preamble: Denasalization of the glottalized alveolar nasal [nˀ] (Americanist n̓) to a glottalized voiced stop [dˀ] (d̓), with the glottalization kept. Werle (2010: 4) sets out the Southern Wakashan correspondences: where Nuu-chah-nulth keeps the nasals m m̓ n n̓, Ditidaht has the voiced stops b b̓ d d̓, while Makah has plain b and d for both, its glottalized resonants having merged with the plain ones with lengthening of the preceding vowel (also Davidson 2002: 76). Wikipedia's Ditidaht consonant table likewise lists glottalized ˀb ˀd alongside ˀm ˀn; Werle (2010: 4) notes that Ditidaht keeps n and n̓ in a few words with diminutive meaning. Werle's word example is 'white person': Nuu-chah-nulth mamałn̓i, Ditidaht babład̓, Makah babałid or babałdi-. Werle (2010: 5), following Gamble (1977), analyses Ditidaht b̓ d̓ as single, fully voiced, pre-glottalized segments that occur only after a vowel, and notes that some speakers reduce them to a glottal stop in casual speech. Other descriptions write them as /ʔb ʔd/ sequences (Swadesh & Swadesh 1933, Thomas & Hess 1981, Powell 1991, Fortescue 2007, Jacobsen 2007, cited by Werle). Word-initially the Ditidaht reflex shown by Werle is plain d: Nuu-chah-nulth n̓uw̓iiqsu, Ditidaht duw̓aqs 'father' (p. 17). For Quileute, Wikipedia's summary of Powell (1974) gives Proto-Chimakuan *n̓ > d or ʔd, a plain d or a glottal stop plus d, and notes that neither Chimakuan language has glottalized resonants synchronically; it cites no word with *n̓. For Lushootseed, the pronunciation guide of Bates, Hess & Hilbert (1994: xii) lists a rare glottalized b̓ that never begins a word, but no d̓. Only one word pair is verified here.

languageExamples.context: Werle (2010: 4–5): Ditidaht has voiced stops b b̓ d d̓ where Nuu-chah-nulth has m m̓ n n̓; b̓ d̓ are pre-glottalized and occur only after a vowel

examples.note: Werle (2010: 4), ex. (5), cited to show that only Ditidaht allows glottalized resonants in codas. Makah babałid, babałdi- has plain d. Both b's of Ditidaht and Makah bab- correspond to the two m's of Nuu-chah-nulth mam-, the plain-nasal change *m > b.
